definition_zh: 硬的；坚固的；困难的；努力的；猛烈地；努力地
definition_en: firm and stiff to touch; difficult to do or understand; with great effort or force
core_image: 攥紧的拳头：握得越紧越用力，也越难被改变
scene: 他反复敲那张旧木桌，声音又闷又沉，木头结实得像石头。He knocked on the old wooden desk again and again; the wood felt hard as stone.
sceneCN: 这里 hard 是「硬的、坚固的」（第 1 个义项：质地坚硬不易变形）；木头结实得像石头，说明它摸起来硬、不易弯曲，属于 hard 最基本的触感义。

derivatives.zh: 使变硬；变硬，由 hard 加动词后缀 -en 构成，表示「变得坚硬」
硬度；坚硬，由 hard 加名词后缀 -ness 构成，指坚硬的性质
几乎不；简直不，由 hard 加副词后缀 -ly 构成，语义弱化为否定

senses.title: Firm and stiff
senses.definition: not soft and difficult to bend, break, or press
senses.definitionCN: 不软，难以弯曲、折断或压扁
senses.example: The ground was hard after weeks without rain.
senses.exampleCN: 几个星期没下雨，地面变硬了。
senses.why: The core image is a clenched fist: something pressed tight resists change, so the physical sense of firmness comes first.
senses.whyCN: 核心意象是攥紧的拳头：被压紧的东西抗拒改变，所以「质地坚硬」成为最直接的身体感受，也是最早的义项。

senses.title: Difficult to do
senses.definition: difficult to do, understand, or answer
senses.definitionCN: 难做、难懂或难回答
senses.example: That was a hard question on the exam.
senses.exampleCN: 那是考试里一道很难的题。
senses.why: When something resists your effort the way stone resists your hand, the feeling of resistance extends to tasks, so hard comes to mean difficult.
senses.whyCN: 当一件事像石头挡住手一样挡住你的努力时，这种「阻力感」就从触感转移到任务上，于是 hard 引申出「困难」义。

senses.title: With great effort
senses.definition: using a lot of effort or energy
senses.definitionCN: 付出大量力气或精力去做
senses.example: She worked hard to finish the project on time.
senses.exampleCN: 她努力工作，按时完成了项目。
senses.why: Doing something difficult requires pushing with force, so the adjective of resistance becomes an adverb of intense effort.
senses.whyCN: 做困难的事需要用大力气去推，表示「有阻力」的形容词由此变成表示「用力、努力」的副词。

senses.title: Severe or harsh
senses.definition: not kind or gentle; treating people in a severe way
senses.definitionCN: 不温和，对待人严厉苛刻
senses.example: The teacher was hard on students who came late.
senses.exampleCN: 老师对迟到的学生很严厉。
senses.why: A surface that gives no comfort feels cold and unyielding, so hard extends to attitudes that give no mercy or gentleness.
senses.whyCN: 不给人舒服余地的表面冷硬不弯，这种感受延伸到人的态度上，就有了「严厉、苛刻」义。

intro.en: Hard is one of the oldest English adjectives, tracing straight back to Germanic roots.
intro.cn: hard 是英语最古老的形容词之一，可以直接追溯到日耳曼语词根。

items.en: Old English had heard, meaning solid and firm, already covering both physical hardness and difficulty.
items.cn: 古英语作 heard，意为「坚固的」，已经同时覆盖「坚硬」和「困难」两个意思。

items.en: It comes from the reconstructed Germanic root *harðuz, shared across the Germanic languages.
items.cn: 它来自重构的日耳曼词根 *harðuz，在各日耳曼语言中广泛共用。

items.en: Old Norse harðr, meaning hard and severe, is a close relative that reinforced the English word.
items.cn: 古诺斯语 harðr 意为「坚硬、严厉」，是英语这个词的近亲，强化了它的用法。

items.en: German hart keeps the same meaning today, showing how stable this root has been.
items.cn: 德语 hart 至今意义相同，可见这个词根非常稳定。

items.en: In Modern English, hard split into the adjectival and adverbial uses, while hardly drifted to mean almost not.
items.cn: 现代英语里，hard 分出形容词与副词用法，而 hardly 则漂移为「几乎不」的意思。

note.en: Words that share the shape or the meaning field of hard.
note.cn: 与 hard 形近或义近的词。

entries.definition: to become or make something hard
entries.definitionCN: 使变硬；硬化，与 hard 同根，加动词后缀 -en
艰难；困苦，同根词，指生活上的艰苦

entries.definition: metal tools and the physical parts of a computer
entries.definitionCN: 五金器具；计算机硬件，hard 与 ware 的合成词

entries.definition: not easy to do or understand
entries.definitionCN: 困难的；不易的，义场相近但词源不同

entries.definition: solid and not likely to change
entries.definitionCN: 坚固的；坚定的，与 hard 第一个义项相近

entries.definition: strong and difficult to break or chew
entries.definitionCN: 坚韧的；难对付的，与 hard 义场重叠

normalIntro.en: Five routes into the word hard.
normalIntro.cn: 五条记住 hard 的路径。

normal.cn: hard 与 hardness：hard 是「硬」，hardness 是「硬度」，同根好记。
短语「hard as stone」（硬得像石头）把触感义锁进画面。
短语「hard question」（难题）把困难义固定下来。
搭配「work hard」（努力工作）锁定副词用法。
hardly 已经漂移成「几乎不」，别把它当成 hard 的普通副词形式。

abstract.en: Picture a fist clenched so tight that nothing can bend it.
abstract.cn: 想象一只攥得死紧的拳头，什么都掰不动它——这就是 hard 的核心画面。

abstract.en: Feel a stone wall refusing your push.
abstract.cn: 感受一堵石墙拒绝你推过去的手掌：阻力感就是 hard 的全部含义。

abstract.en: Link the resistance of stone to the resistance of a task.
abstract.cn: 把石头的阻力接到任务的阻力上：硬的东西难推动，难的事 hard to do。

examples.en: The bread had gone hard after two days in the open air.
examples.cn: 面包在露天放了两天，已经变硬了。

examples.en: It is hard to keep a secret when everyone is asking questions.
examples.cn: 当所有人都在追问时，保守秘密很难。

examples.en: He trains hard every morning before school.
examples.cn: 他每天早晨上学前都刻苦训练。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「哈的」——敲桌子敲得「哈」一声，因为桌面是硬的；硬的东西难推，难的事要努力干。

root: hard 来自原始日耳曼语词根 *harðuz（坚硬），古英语作 heard。这个词根在日耳曼语系中高度稳定，德语 hart 与之同源。词义从「质地坚硬」自然引申为「困难」「用力」「严厉」，属于典型的触感隐喻扩展。

sensesIntro.en: The senses move from physical firmness to difficulty, effort, and severity.
sensesIntro.cn: 义项从身体的坚硬感出发，延伸到困难、用力与严厉。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a clenched fist that nothing can bend
core.cn: 核心意象：攥紧的拳头，什么都掰不动

branches.cn: 同一种阻力感，分出触感与任务两界

intro.en: Hard forms a small but productive Germanic family.
intro.cn: hard 构成一个规模不大但能产的日耳曼词族。

latinIntro.en: Hard is Germanic, so there are no Latin relatives here.
latinIntro.cn: hard 属日耳曼词源，没有拉丁同族词。

definition_en: almost not; only just; certainly not
core_image: 门缝里漏进的一线光：光照了，但少得几乎看不见
scene: 考完试他累得说不出一句完整的话，回答时几乎不抬眼皮。He was so tired after the exam that he hardly spoke during dinner.
sceneCN: 这里 hardly 是「几乎不」（第 1 个义项：程度极低近乎否定）；晚饭时他累得几乎不开口，hardly 把动词说话的意义压到几乎为零。

derivatives.zh: 硬的；困难的，hardly 的基础词，语义本为坚硬或困难
硬度；坚硬，同根名词，指坚硬的性质
耐寒的；强壮的，同根形容词，指能吃苦耐寒

senses.title: Almost not
senses.definition: almost not at all; only a very small amount
senses.definitionCN: 几乎完全不；程度极小
senses.example: There was hardly any food left in the fridge.
senses.exampleCN: 冰箱里几乎没剩下什么食物。
senses.why: Hard originally means with force, and pressing an action down to almost nothing flips the sense into near negation.
senses.whyCN: hard 本义与「用力」相关，把一个动作压到几乎为零，语义便翻转成近乎否定的「几乎不」。

senses.title: Only just
senses.definition: only just; not more than
senses.definitionCN: 仅仅；不超过
senses.example: She had hardly sat down when the phone rang.
senses.exampleCN: 她刚坐下电话就响了。
senses.why: When almost nothing of an action is complete, the time line shows the event barely finished, giving the sense of barely or only just.
senses.whyCN: 当一个动作只完成了一丁点，时间线上就呈现出「勉强完成」，于是有了「刚刚才」的时间义。

intro.en: Hardly grew from the adverbial use of hard and then flipped its meaning.
intro.cn: hardly 由 hard 的副词用法长出，后来语义发生翻转。

items.en: The adjective hard took the adverb suffix -lice to form heardlice, meaning in a hard manner or severely.
items.cn: 古英语形容词 hard 加副词后缀 -lice 构成 heardlice，意为「以强硬的方式、严厉地」。

items.en: In Middle English, hardly still meant boldly or with force, close to the modern word hardly at all.
items.cn: 中古英语里 hardly 仍表示「大胆地、用力地」，与今天的意思相去甚远。

items.en: By the fifteenth century the sense weakened, and hardly came to mean barely or almost not.
items.cn: 到十五世纪，词义弱化，hardly 逐渐表示「勉强地、几乎不」。

items.en: Modern grammars treat hardly as a negative adverb, pairing it with any instead of some.
items.cn: 现代语法把 hardly 视为否定副词，句中要配 any 而不是 some。

items.en: The phrase hardly ever fixed itself as the standard way to say almost never.
items.cn: 短语 hardly ever 固定下来，成为表示「几乎从不」的标准说法。

note.en: Look-alikes and meaning neighbours of hardly.
note.cn: hardly 的形近词与义近词。

entries.definitionCN: 硬的；困难的；努力地，同根基础词
艰难；困苦，同根名词
耐寒的；强壮的，同根形容词，拼写相近
仅仅；几乎不，义场几乎重合
几乎不；决不，近义副词
很少；不常，与 hardly ever 的频度义相近

normalIntro.en: Five ways to lock in hardly.
normalIntro.cn: 五个角度锁定 hardly。

normal.cn: 搭配「hardly any」（几乎没有）是最常见的量级否定。
搭配「hardly ever」（几乎从不）锁定频度用法。
hard 加 -ly 后语义弱化成否定，别按字面理解成「努力地」。
hardly 是否定词，句中配 any 不配 some。
句型「hardly ... when ...」表示「刚……就……」。

abstract.en: Picture light leaking through a door crack: present but almost invisible.
abstract.cn: 想象门缝里漏进的一线光：存在，但几乎看不见——这就是 hardly 的量。

abstract.en: Feel an action pressed down to almost zero.
abstract.cn: 感受一个动作被压到几乎为零：hardly 把动词的分量压扁。

abstract.en: See someone just touching the chair as the phone rings.
abstract.cn: 看到一个人刚碰到椅子电话就响：hardly 表示「刚刚才」。

examples.en: I could hardly hear the teacher from the back row.
examples.cn: 从最后一排我几乎听不见老师的声音。

examples.en: There is hardly any milk left in the bottle.
examples.cn: 瓶子里几乎没剩什么牛奶。

examples.en: She hardly ever watches television these days.
examples.cn: 她这几天几乎从不看电视。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「哈的利」——问「哈的利索吗？」答「几乎不利索」：hardly 的意思就是几乎不、简直不。

root: hardly 由 hard（坚硬、用力）加古英语副词后缀 -ly（-lice）构成，本义为「以强硬的方式」。词义在英语史中逐渐弱化，从「用力」到「勉强」再到「几乎不」，属于常见的否定化漂移。

sensesIntro.en: Hardly covers near-negation and the idea of only just.
sensesIntro.cn: hardly 覆盖「近乎否定」与「刚刚才」两层意思。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a crack of light that is almost too faint to see
core.cn: 核心意象：一线光，弱得几乎看不见

branches.en: An action reduced to almost nothing
branches.cn: 被压到几乎为零的动作

branches.en: An event that has just barely happened

branches.cn: 量极少与时间极短同源
刚完成就被打断的句型感受

intro.en: Hardly is built with the Germanic adverb suffix -ly.
intro.cn: hardly 用日耳曼副词后缀 -ly 构成。

latinIntro.en: Hardly has no Latin relatives; its family is Germanic.
latinIntro.cn: hardly 没有拉丁同族词，词族属日耳曼源。

definition_en: causing or likely to cause harm or damage
core_image: 玻璃碴混进米饭：吃下去就会割伤身体的东西
scene: 工厂把污水排进小河，下游的鱼越来越少，村民都明白这水有毒。The factory dumped dirty water into the river, which was harmful to the fish.
sceneCN: 这里 harmful 是「有害的」（第 1 个义项：对健康或生命造成损害）；脏水毒害鱼群，harmful 直接描述这种造成伤害的性质。

derivatives.zh: 伤害；损害，harmful 的基础名词，指实际的伤害
有害地，由 harmful 加副词后缀 -ly 构成
无害的，由 harm 加后缀 -less 构成，表示没有伤害

senses.title: Causing damage to health or life
senses.definition: causing physical injury or damage to health
senses.definitionCN: 造成身体伤害或损害健康
senses.example: Smoking is harmful to your lungs.
senses.exampleCN: 吸烟对你的肺有害。
senses.why: Harm means injury, and adding the suffix -ful turns a noun of injury into an adjective of cause: something full of harm.
senses.whyCN: harm 意为伤害，加后缀 -ful 把「伤害」名词变成「充满伤害」的形容词，于是指造成伤害的事物。

senses.title: Damaging in effect or influence
senses.definition: having a bad effect on a situation, person, or thing
senses.definitionCN: 对局面、人或事物产生坏影响
senses.example: Spreading rumors is harmful to team trust.
senses.exampleCN: 散布谣言对团队信任有害。
senses.why: Injury is not only physical; the image of cutting and breaking extends to trust, reputation, and relationships.
senses.whyCN: 伤害不限于身体，「割裂、破坏」的意象延伸到信任、名声与关系，harmful 由此覆盖抽象损害。

intro.en: Harmful is built from the old word harm plus the adjective suffix -ful.
intro.cn: harmful 由古词 harm 加形容词后缀 -ful 构成。

items.en: Old English hearm meant injury, evil, or pain, and was already a common word in poetry and law.
items.cn: 古英语 hearm 意为「伤害、恶、痛苦」，在诗歌与法律文本中已很常用。

items.en: It goes back to a Germanic root meaning to shame or injure, shared with Old Saxon harm and Old High German harm.
items.cn: 它可追溯到日耳曼词根，意为「羞辱、伤害」，与古撒克逊语 harm 等同源。

items.en: In Middle English, harm was both noun and verb, and the compound harm-doing described injury in action.
items.cn: 中古英语中 harm 兼作名词与动词，复合词 harm-doing 描述正在进行的伤害。

items.en: The suffix -ful, from Old English full, turned nouns into adjectives meaning full of.
items.cn: 后缀 -ful 来自古英语 full，把名词变成「充满……的」形容词。

items.en: Modern English fixed harmful as the standard adjective for things that cause damage to health or nature.
items.cn: 现代英语把 harmful 固定为描述损害健康或自然的事物标准形容词。

note.en: Words shaped like or close in meaning to harmful.
note.cn: 与 harmful 形近或义近的词。

entries.definitionCN: 伤害；损害，同根基础名词
无害的，同根反义形容词
有害地，同根副词
造成损害的，义场相近
有毒的，特指毒性损害
造成伤害的，正式用语，词源不同

normalIntro.en: Five anchors for the word harmful.
normalIntro.cn: 记住 harmful 的五个锚点。

normal.cn: 结构「harm + -ful」：充满伤害，即有害。
搭配「harmful to health」（有害健康）是最常见用法。
对比例「harmful vs harmless」（有害 vs 无害），后缀决定方向。
短语「harmful effects」（有害影响）把抽象义固定下来。
先记 harm（伤害），再记 harmful（有害的），顺序自然。

abstract.en: See glass shards mixed into rice: eating means getting cut.
abstract.cn: 想象玻璃碴混进米饭：吃下去就会被割伤——这就是 harmful 的画面。

abstract.en: Feel smoke filling a clean room and making people cough.
abstract.cn: 感受烟雾充满洁净房间、让人咳嗽：有害之物正在充满环境。

abstract.en: Extend the cut from skin to trust.
abstract.cn: 把「割伤」从皮肤延伸到信任：谣言也是 harmful。

examples.en: Doctors say too much salt is harmful to the heart.
examples.cn: 医生说过多的盐对心脏有害。

examples.en: The harmful gases from the factory made the nearby trees die.
examples.cn: 工厂排出的有害气体让附近的树木枯死了。

examples.en: Reading in dim light is less harmful than people think.
examples.cn: 在昏暗光线下看书并不像人们想的那么有害。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「哈姆服」——吃了变质的火腿，「哈姆」让你难受，因为它是 harmful（有害的）。

root: harmful 由 harm（伤害，古英语 hearm，源自日耳曼词根「羞辱、伤害」）加形容词后缀 -ful（充满）构成，字面即「充满伤害的」。同族词还有 harmlessly、harmlessness 等。

sensesIntro.en: The word moves from bodily injury to damage in abstract fields.
sensesIntro.cn: 词义从身体伤害延伸到抽象领域的损害。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: glass shards hidden in food
core.cn: 核心意象：藏在食物里的玻璃碴

branches.en: Things that injure health or body
branches.cn: 损害健康与身体的事物

branches.en: Influences that erode trust or value
branches.cn: 侵蚀信任或价值的影响

branches.en: One root image: cutting and breaking
branches.cn: 同一根意象：割裂与破坏
腐蚀关系的谣言与习惯

intro.en: Harmful shows the productive English pattern harm plus suffix.
intro.cn: harmful 展示了 harm 加后缀的高能产英语构词模式。

latinIntro.en: Harm is Germanic, so no Latin relatives belong here.
latinIntro.cn: harm 为日耳曼词源，没有拉丁同族词。

definition_zh: 帽子；（表示职业、角色的）头衔
definition_en: a covering you wear on your head; a role or job shown by a symbol
core_image: 挂在门口衣架上的圆顶帽子：伸手就能拿起来戴上
scene: 下雨了，他出门前从衣架上取下那顶灰色帽子扣在头上。It started to rain, so he put on his hat before leaving.
sceneCN: 这里 hat 是「帽子」（第 1 个义项：戴在头上的遮盖物）；出门下雨戴帽子挡雨，正是 hat 最日常的用法。

derivatives.zh: 不戴帽子的，由 hat 加后缀 -less 构成，表示没有帽子
帽带，由 hat 与 band 合成，指帽子上围绕的一圈带子
帽盒，由 hat 与 box 合成，指装帽子的盒子

senses.title: A covering for the head
senses.definition: a thing you wear on your head for protection or style
senses.definitionCN: 戴在头上用于保护或装饰的东西
senses.example: She bought a wide-brimmed hat for the beach.
senses.exampleCN: 她买了一顶宽檐帽去海边。
senses.why: The most basic human need near the head is protection from sun, rain, and cold, so the word names any shaped head covering.
senses.whyCN: 头部最基本的需求是挡日晒雨淋和御寒，所以这个词泛指一切有形状的头饰。

senses.title: A role or job
senses.definition: a role or job, especially one shown by what you wear or do
senses.definitionCN: 一种角色或职务，常以穿戴或行为体现
senses.example: At work he wears his manager hat, at home his father hat.
senses.exampleCN: 工作时他是经理，回家后是父亲。
senses.why: Uniforms and headgear historically marked professions, so the image of putting on a hat became a symbol of taking on a role.

intro.en: Hat is a short Germanic word with a long history on people's heads.
intro.cn: hat 是一个简短的日耳曼词，长期与人们的头顶相伴。

items.en: Old English hatt meant a head covering, already distinct from helmet or hood.
items.cn: 古英语 hatt 意为「头饰」，已与头盔、兜帽相区分。

items.en: It traces to a Germanic root meaning to cover or hide, related to the idea of shading the head.
items.cn: 它可追溯到日耳曼词根，意为「覆盖、遮藏」，与遮蔽头部的意象相关。

items.en: Old Norse hottr, meaning a hood or cap, is a close relative in the northern languages.
items.cn: 古诺斯语 hottr 意为「兜帽或便帽」，是北方语言中的近亲。

items.en: In Middle English, hat covered everything from straw caps to fine felt crowns of rank.
items.cn: 中古英语里，hat 涵盖从草帽到标识身份的精美毡帽。

items.en: Modern English extended hat into idioms like hats off and old hat for old-fashioned things.
items.cn: 现代英语把 hat 扩展进 hats off、old hat 等习语。

definition_en: to feel very strong dislike for someone or something
core_image: 背过身去推开碗：连看都不想看一眼的强烈排斥
scene: 弟弟最讨厌吃芹菜，一闻到那股味道就把碗推得远远的。He hates celery so much that he pushes the bowl away at once.
sceneCN: 这里 hate 是「讨厌、厌恶」（第 1 个义项：强烈不喜欢）；弟弟一闻到味道就推开碗，正是 hate 表示强烈反感的日常用法。

derivatives.zh: 憎恨；仇恨，由 hate 加名词后缀构成的强义名词
可恶的；充满仇恨的，由 hate 加后缀 -ful 构成
怀恨者；反对者，由 hate 加施动者后缀 -er 构成

senses.title: To dislike strongly
senses.definition: to feel a very strong dislike for something or someone
senses.definitionCN: 对某人或某事感到强烈的不喜欢
senses.example: I hate getting up early on cold mornings.
senses.exampleCN: 我讨厌在寒冷的早晨早起。
senses.why: The core image is pushing a bowl away: the body turns from the object, so hate names the strongest form of dislike.
senses.whyCN: 核心意象是推开碗：身体背对对象，hate 因此表示不喜欢情绪的最强形式。

senses.title: To feel intense hostility
senses.definition: to feel extreme anger and hostility toward a person or group
senses.definitionCN: 对某人或某群体感到极端的愤怒与敌意
senses.example: He hated the men who had destroyed his family.
senses.exampleCN: 他憎恨那些毁掉他家庭的人。
senses.why: When dislike is fed by pain and memory, it hardens into hostility, and hate becomes a settled emotion rather than a passing mood.
senses.whyCN: 当反感被痛苦和记忆喂养，它就硬化成敌意，hate 由一时情绪变成持久的情感状态。

senses.title: To regret or be sorry
senses.definition: used to say politely that you are sorry to do something
senses.definitionCN: 礼貌地表示不愿做某事
senses.example: I hate to trouble you, but could you help me?
senses.exampleCN: 我很不愿打扰你，但能帮个忙吗？
senses.why: Because strong dislike includes wanting to avoid something, polite English borrows the word to express reluctance to impose.
senses.whyCN: 强烈反感包含「想回避」，礼貌英语借这个词表达不愿打扰对方的客气。

intro.en: Hate runs through Germanic languages as the word for strong dislike.
intro.cn: hate 贯穿各日耳曼语言，是表示强烈厌恶的词。

items.en: Old English had the verb hatian, meaning to hate or hold as an enemy.
items.cn: 古英语动词 hatian，意为「憎恨、视之为敌」。

items.en: It comes from a Germanic root *hataz, the standard word for hostility in the family.
items.cn: 它来自日耳曼词根 *hataz，是日耳曼语族中表示敌意的标准词。

items.en: Old Norse hata reinforced the English verb after Viking settlements.
items.cn: 维京人定居后，古诺斯语 hata 强化了英语的这个动词。

items.en: In Middle English, hate appeared widely as both verb and noun in songs and chronicles.
items.cn: 中古英语中，hate 以动词与名词两种身份广泛出现在诗歌与编年史里。

items.en: Modern English added compounds like hate speech and hate crime for hostility turned into action.
items.cn: 现代英语新增 hate speech、hate crime 等复合词，描述化为行动的敌意。

note.en: Look-alikes and neighbours in the dislike field.
note.cn: hate 的形近词与厌恶义场的近邻。

abstract.en: Feel yourself turning your back so you need not look.

definition_en: to own or hold something; to do or take an action; used with a past participle to make perfect tenses
core_image: 摊开的手掌：东西就在你手里握着
scene: 书包里装着他新买的字典，随时可以拿出来查。He has a new dictionary in his schoolbag.
sceneCN: 这里 have 是「有、拥有」（第 1 个义项：所有与持有）；书包里的字典属于他、随时可用，正是 have 表示拥有的基本用法。

senses.title: To own or possess
senses.definition: to own something or have it as your own
senses.definitionCN: 拥有某物或作为自己的东西持有
senses.example: They have a small garden behind the house.
senses.exampleCN: 他们在房子后面有个小花园。
senses.why: The image is an open palm holding something, so have first names the state of keeping things in hand.
senses.whyCN: 意象是摊开的手掌握住东西，have 最初命名的是「把东西握在手里」的状态。

senses.title: To do or take an action
senses.definition: to perform or experience an action or event
senses.definitionCN: 做出或经历某个动作、事件
senses.example: We had a long meeting this afternoon.
senses.exampleCN: 我们今天下午开了一个很长的会。
senses.why: Possession extends to experiences: what you hold includes activities, so have pairs with nouns to mean doing them.
senses.whyCN: 「持有」延伸到「经历」：你握着的也可以是活动，have 与名词搭配即表示做这件事。

senses.title: To eat or drink
senses.definition: to eat or drink something
senses.definitionCN: 吃或喝某种东西
senses.example: She had tea with her grandmother.
senses.exampleCN: 她和祖母一起喝了茶。
senses.why: Taking food into the body is another way of holding or receiving it, so have covers meals and drinks.
senses.whyCN: 把食物纳入身体也是一种「接收、握取」，于是 have 覆盖饮食场合。

senses.title: Auxiliary for perfect tenses
senses.definition: used with a past participle to form the perfect tenses
senses.definitionCN: 与过去分词连用构成完成时态
senses.example: I have finished my homework already.
senses.exampleCN: 我已经做完了作业。
senses.why: Possession extends to time: an action you have done belongs to you like an object you hold.
senses.whyCN: 「拥有」延伸到时间：已经完成的动作像握在手里的物品一样归属于你，have 由此成为完成时助动词。

intro.en: Have is one of the most basic verbs in English, inherited directly from Germanic.
intro.cn: have 是英语最基础的动词之一，直接继承自日耳曼语。

items.en: Old English habban meant to hold, own, or possess, already very common in speech.
items.cn: 古英语 habban 意为「持有、拥有」，口语中已极为常用。

items.en: It comes from the Germanic root *habjan, shared with German haben and Dutch hebben.
items.cn: 它来自日耳曼词根 *habjan，与德语 haben、荷兰语 hebben 同源。

items.en: Old Norse hafa helped shape the modern short form of the verb.
items.cn: 古诺斯语 hafa 对现代动词的简短形式起了塑造作用。

items.en: In Middle English, have developed the auxiliary use with past participles, replacing older periphrases.
items.cn: 中古英语中，have 与过去分词连用的助动词用法发展起来，取代了旧有的表达。

items.en: Modern English added many idioms such as have to and have got, deepening its daily use.
items.cn: 现代英语发展出 have to、have got 等大量习语，使其日常用法更加丰富。

scene: 操场上站着几个孩子，老师说穿蓝衣服的那位跑得最快。He runs faster than anyone else in the class.
sceneCN: 这里 he 是「他」（第 1 个义项：指代前文提到的男性）；老师接着用 he 指代那个穿蓝衣服的男生，是 he 的基本指代用法。

senses.title: The male person mentioned

senses.example: Tom is my cousin, and he lives in Guangzhou.
senses.exampleCN: 汤姆是我表哥，他住在广州。
senses.why: When a male has been named, the mind points back to him, so he acts as the pointing word for that man.
senses.whyCN: 当男性被点名后，说话人心里的手指向他，he 就是用来指向那个人的代词。

senses.title: Any male person
senses.titleCN: 任何一个男性；泛指男性
senses.definition: a male person in general; anyone male
senses.definitionCN: 泛指的男性；任何男性
senses.example: He who works hard will succeed.
senses.exampleCN: 努力工作的人会成功。
senses.why: When no particular man is named, he stands for males in general, turning one pointing word into a general label.
senses.whyCN: 当没有具体指名时，he 泛指男性，使一个指示词变成概括性标签。

senses.title: Person of unknown sex in older style
senses.definition: used in older English for a person whose sex is not known
senses.definitionCN: 旧式英语中指性别不明的人
senses.example: If anyone calls, tell him I am busy.
senses.exampleCN: 如果有人打电话，告诉他我在忙。
senses.why: Older English defaulted to the male pronoun when sex was unknown, though modern usage prefers they.
senses.whyCN: 旧式英语在性别不明时默认用男性代词，现代用法更倾向用 they。

items.en: Old English had he, the same shape as today, with forms hi, him, and his.
items.cn: 古英语就已作 he，与今天拼写相同，另有 hi、him、his 等形式。

items.en: It comes from the Germanic demonstrative root *hiz, meaning this one over there.
items.cn: 它来自日耳曼指示词根 *hiz，意为「那边那一个」。

items.en: The root traces further back to the reconstructed form *ki- or *ko-, the base of many pointing words.
items.cn: 词根可再上溯到重构形式 *ki- 或 *ko-，是许多指示词的基础。

items.en: In Middle English, the forms he and hi competed before the modern set settled.

items.en: Modern English uses he mainly for males, with they increasingly used for unknown sex.

normalIntro.cn: 记住代词 he 的五个锚点。

normal.cn: 搭配「he is」（他是）是最基本的句型。
对比「he vs she」：性别是两个词唯一的核心区别。
宾格 him 用于动词和介词之后。
所有格 his 既可作形容词性也可作名词性。
反身形式 himself 强调「他本人」。

abstract.en: See a hand pointing at one boy in a group.
abstract.cn: 看见一只手指向人群中的那个男孩：he 就是那根手指。

abstract.en: Follow the arrow back to the name just spoken.
abstract.cn: 让箭头回指刚说过的名字：代词是记忆的指针。

abstract.en: Say his name once, then let he do the work.
abstract.cn: 名字说一次，后面让 he 接班，避免重复。

examples.en: My father is a doctor, and he works at a local hospital.
examples.cn: 我父亲是医生，他在当地一家医院工作。

examples.en: He who asks questions learns twice as fast.
examples.cn: 爱提问的人学得快一倍。

examples.en: Everyone should bring his own lunch to the trip.
examples.cn: 每个人都应自带午餐去旅行。（旧式用法）

dict_mnemonic.text: 「嘿」——喊一声「嘿！」，那个人回头，he 就是指那个「他」。

root: he 来自古英语 hē，源自日耳曼指示词根 *hiz，更早可上溯至原始印欧语 *ki-/*ko-（指示词基）。同族形式覆盖整个德语系指示代词系统，德语 er、荷兰语 hij 为同源对应。

sensesIntro.en: From pointing at a known male to covering males in general.
sensesIntro.cn: 从指向已知的男性到泛指男性。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand pointing at one man in a group
core.cn: 核心意象：指向人群中一位男性的手

branches.en: The old default for unknown sex
branches.cn: 旧式英语对性别不明者的默认指代
同一根指针，指向具体与泛指
让对话避免重复的指代功能

intro.en: He anchors the whole male pronoun set.
intro.cn: he 是整套男性代词形式的核心。

latinIntro.en: He is Germanic, so no Latin relatives belong here.
latinIntro.cn: he 属日耳曼词源，没有拉丁同族词。

definition_zh: 头；头部；头脑；负责人；顶部；前进；领导
definition_en: the part of the body above the neck; the mind; the person in charge; the top of something; to move forward
core_image: 身体最上端的指挥台：五官俱全、发号施令的位置
scene: 全班同学抬头看黑板顶端那行字，班长站在最前面带读。The students looked up, and the teacher stood at the head of the classroom.
sceneCN: 这里 head 是「顶部；最前面」（第 2 个义项：位置的最高点或最前端）；老师站在教室最前端，正是 head 表示位置义的用法。

derivatives.zh: 标题；头条新闻，由 head 与 line 合成，指报纸顶端的文字
头痛，由 head 与 ache 合成，指头部疼痛
在前面；向前，由 a 与 head 合成，表示位置在前

senses.title: The part of the body
senses.definition: the part of the body containing the brain, eyes, and mouth
senses.definitionCN: 身体上包含脑、眼、口的部位
senses.example: She nodded her head in agreement.
senses.exampleCN: 她点头表示同意。
senses.why: The most visible and vital part of the body stands at the top, so the word first names that physical part.
senses.whyCN: 身体最显眼、最关键的部分位于顶端，这个词首先命名这个身体部位。

senses.title: The top or front position
senses.definition: the highest or most forward part of something
senses.definitionCN: 事物最高或最前的部分
senses.example: Write your name at the head of the page.
senses.exampleCN: 把名字写在页面顶端。
senses.why: Since the head sits at the top of the body, the word naturally extends to the top or front of anything.
senses.whyCN: 既然头位于身体顶端，这个词自然延伸到任何事物的顶部或前端。

senses.title: The mind or thinking
senses.definition: the mind; the ability to think
senses.definitionCN: 头脑；思维能力
senses.example: A good head for numbers helps in maths.
senses.exampleCN: 擅长数学需要很好的数感。
senses.why: The brain lives inside the head, so the word carries the power of thought inside it.
senses.whyCN: 大脑住在头颅里，这个词于是承载了思维的含义。

senses.title: The person in charge
senses.definition: the person who leads or directs a group
senses.definitionCN: 领导或指挥一个团体的人
senses.example: The head of the school welcomed the new teachers.
senses.exampleCN: 校长欢迎了新老师。
senses.why: The leader directs the group like the head directs the body, so the image maps onto authority.
senses.whyCN: 领袖指挥团体就像头部指挥身体，这个意象自然映射到职权上。

senses.title: To move in a direction
senses.definition: to move or go in a particular direction
senses.definitionCN: 朝特定方向移动
senses.example: We headed home before the storm arrived.
senses.exampleCN: 暴风雨来之前我们朝家赶去。
senses.why: The body is led by the head, so moving forward takes the word of the part that leads.
senses.whyCN: 身体由头部引领前行，于是「朝某方向去」借用了领头部位的名字。

intro.en: Head is a native English word with a rich history of extension.
intro.cn: head 是英语本土词，词义扩展史十分丰富。

items.en: Old English heafod meant the head and already the chief part or leader.
items.cn: 古英语 heafod 意为「头」，已兼指首要部分或领袖。

items.en: It comes from the Germanic root *haubudam, meaning chief part of the body.
items.cn: 它来自日耳曼词根 *haubudam，意为「身体的首要部分」。

items.en: Related forms appear in Low German hovet and Dutch hoofd.
items.cn: 低地德语 hovet 与荷兰语 hoofd 是同族形式。

items.en: In Middle English the spelling varied widely before head became standard.
items.cn: 中古英语拼写形式多样，最终 head 成为标准形式。

items.en: Modern English extended head into compounds like headline and headphones.
items.cn: 现代英语把 head 扩展进 headline、headphones 等复合词。

note.en: Look-alikes and meaning neighbours of head.
note.cn: head 的形近词与义近词。

normalIntro.en: Five ways to keep head in place.
normalIntro.cn: 五个方式把 head 记牢。

normal.cn: 搭配「shake one's head」（摇头）是最常用的身体动作短语。
短语「at the head of」（在……最前面）锁定位置义。
对比「head vs brain」：head 是整个头部，brain 只是器官。
搭配「head for」（朝……去）记住动词用法。
复合词「headmaster」（校长）体现 head 的领导义。

abstract.en: See a command post at the very top of the body.
abstract.cn: 看见身体最顶端的指挥台：五官发令、身体执行，head 就是司令部。

abstract.en: Map the head onto the top of a page or a line.
abstract.cn: 把头映射到页面顶端或队伍排头：位置义由此而来。

abstract.en: Feel yourself leaning forward and leading the line.
abstract.cn: 感受自己探身走在队伍最前：head for 就是朝那个方向去。

examples.en: He shook his head when I offered him more cake.
examples.cn: 我问他还要不要蛋糕时，他摇了摇头。

examples.en: The head of the team made the final decision.
examples.cn: 团队负责人做了最后决定。

examples.en: We are heading to the museum this weekend.
examples.cn: 这个周末我们要去博物馆。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「海德」——巨人「海德」个子太高，别人只能看见他的头：head 就是头。

root: head 来自古英语 heafod，源自日耳曼词根 *haubudam（身体首要部分），与荷兰语 hoofd、德语 Haupt 同源。词义从身体部位扩展到位置顶端、心智与领袖，是英语中扩展最丰富的本土词之一。

sensesIntro.en: From the top of the body to the top of everything.
sensesIntro.cn: 从身体的顶端到万物的顶端。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: the command post at the top of the body
core.cn: 核心意象：身体最顶端的指挥台

branches.en: The top or front of things
The head leads, so movement follows
branches.cn: 头引领方向，身体的移动由此得名

intro.en: Head is a tireless compound builder.
intro.cn: head 是极其能产的复合词构词成分。

latinIntro.en: Head is Germanic, so Latin relatives are absent here.
latinIntro.cn: head 属日耳曼词源，没有拉丁同族词。

definition_en: a pain in the head; a problem that causes worry
core_image: 太阳穴里的小锤子：一下一下敲着同一处
scene: 他熬夜复习到凌晨，早读时太阳穴突突地跳。He went to the nurse because of a bad headache.
sceneCN: 这里 headache 是「头痛」（第 1 个义项：头部的疼痛）；熬夜后太阳穴跳疼，headache 直接描述这种身体不适。

derivatives.zh: 头，headache 的基础词
疼痛，headache 的第二个构成成分，指持续隐痛
胃痛，同类复合词， ache 前换部位

senses.title: Pain in the head
senses.definition: a pain felt inside or around the head
senses.definitionCN: 头部内或周围的疼痛感
senses.example: Loud music gave her a splitting headache.
senses.exampleCN: 吵闹的音乐让她头痛欲裂。
senses.why: Ache means a dull continuing pain, and fixing it to the head names the commonest of all minor pains.
senses.whyCN: ache 指持续的隐痛，固定到 head 上，就命名了最常见的小病痛。

senses.title: An annoying problem
senses.definition: a problem that is difficult and worrying
senses.definitionCN: 棘手而令人烦心的问题
senses.example: The traffic jam is a real headache for drivers.
senses.exampleCN: 交通拥堵对司机来说实在令人头痛。
senses.why: A persistent worry keeps knocking like the pain keeps knocking, so trouble borrows the image of pain.
senses.whyCN: 持续烦心事像疼痛一样一下一下敲人，麻烦事由此借用疼痛的意象。

intro.en: Headache is a transparent compound built from two native words.
intro.cn: headache 是由两个本族词构成的透明复合词。

items.en: Old English had heafodece, combining head with ache.
items.cn: 古英语作 heafodece，由 head 与 ache 复合而成。

items.en: The word ache came from Old English acan, meaning to suffer continuous pain.
items.cn: ache 一词来自古英语 acan，意为「持续疼痛」。

items.en: In Middle English, headache was recorded for both the pain and, later, the figurative trouble.
items.cn: 中古英语里 headache 既记录了疼痛义，后来也有了比喻的麻烦义。

items.en: Related compounds such as toothache and stomachache formed in the same period.
items.cn: toothache、stomachache 等同类复合词也在同期形成。

items.en: Modern English kept headache as the standard word for both physical pain and daily annoyances.
items.cn: 现代英语把 headache 保留为身体疼痛与日常麻烦的标准词。

note.en: Look-alikes and pain-family neighbours.
note.cn: headache 的形近词与疼痛家族近邻。

疼痛，复合词的第二个成分

偏头痛，特指反复发作的剧烈头痛
牙痛，同族复合词
麻烦，与第二义项相近

normalIntro.en: Five anchors for headache.
normalIntro.cn: 记住 headache 的五个锚点。

normal.cn: 结构「head + ache」（头 + 痛）字面即可读出词义。
搭配「have a headache」（头痛）是最常见表达。
短语「splitting headache」（头痛欲裂）形容程度。
同法记忆 toothache、stomachache：部位 + ache。
比喻用法「a real headache」（真麻烦事）拓展词义。

abstract.en: Feel a tiny hammer tapping inside the temple.
abstract.cn: 感受太阳穴里的小锤子一下一下敲：这就是 ache 的节奏。

abstract.en: Let the tapping continue all day like a worry.
abstract.cn: 让敲击延续一整天，如同烦心事挥之不去：比喻义由此生长。

abstract.en: Swap the body part to build new words.
abstract.cn: 换掉部位就能造新词：tooth、stomach、heart + ache。

examples.en: I have a headache and want to lie down for a while.
examples.cn: 我有点头痛，想躺一会儿。

examples.en: The new tax forms are a headache for small businesses.
examples.cn: 新的报税表格让小企业头疼不已。

examples.en: A cold shower cured his headache quickly.
examples.cn: 冲了个凉水澡，他的头痛很快就好了。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「海德爱科」——学生「海德」爱熬夜，科科熬夜就 headache（头痛）。

root: headache 由 head（头，古英语 heafod）与 ache（持续疼痛，古英语 acan）复合而成，古英语已见 heafodece 形式。同族复合词有 toothache、stomachache、backache、heartache 等，构词能产。

sensesIntro.en: From a pain in the head to a pain in daily life.
sensesIntro.cn: 从头部的疼痛到日常生活的烦忧。

core.cn: 核心意象：太阳穴里一下一下敲的小锤子

branches.cn: ache 表示的持续性隐痛

intro.en: Headache belongs to the ache family of compounds.
intro.cn: headache 属于 ache 复合词家族。

latinIntro.en: Both parts are native English, so no Latin relatives exist here.
latinIntro.cn: 两个成分都是英语本族词，没有拉丁同族词。

definition_zh: 健康；健康状况；医疗；卫生
definition_en: the condition of your body and mind; how well someone is
core_image: 一棵浇水施肥后枝繁叶茂的树：状态良好、充满生机
scene: 体测那天他跑步、跳绳样样达标，医生夸他身体棒。Good food and exercise keep him in good health.
sceneCN: 这里 health 是「健康」（第 1 个义项：身体与精神的良好状态）；饮食加锻炼让他状态良好，health 描述这种整体良好状况。

derivatives.zh: 健康的，由 health 加形容词后缀 -y 构成
健康地，由 healthy 加副词后缀 -ly 构成
治愈；愈合，与 health 同族，指使恢复健康

senses.title: The condition of body and mind
senses.definition: the general condition of a person's body and mind
senses.definitionCN: 一个人身体与精神的总体状况
senses.example: Regular sleep is the key to good health.
senses.exampleCN: 规律睡眠是健康的关键。
senses.why: The whole person runs well or badly like a machine, so health names that overall running state.
senses.whyCN: 整个人像机器一样运转良好或欠佳，health 命名的就是这种整体运转状态。

senses.title: The state of an organization or system
senses.definition: how well something such as a company or economy is doing
senses.definitionCN: 公司、经济等运行的好坏程度
senses.example: The doctor examined the financial health of the firm.
senses.exampleCN: 医生检查了公司财务的「健康状况」。
senses.why: A body that runs well becomes a system that runs well, so the word extends to organizations and economies.
senses.whyCN: 运转良好的身体映射到运转良好的系统，health 由此延伸到机构与经济。

senses.title: Medical work and public care
senses.definition: the work of treating and preventing illness
senses.definitionCN: 治疗与预防疾病的工作
senses.example: She works in the health service.
senses.exampleCN: 她在医疗卫生系统工作。
senses.why: Keeping bodies well becomes an institution, so health names the whole field of care.
senses.whyCN: 让身体保持良好状态发展成一项事业，health 由此命名整个医疗领域。

intro.en: Health grows from the same root as whole and heal.
intro.cn: health 与 whole、heal 同根而生。

items.en: Old English hælth came from hal, meaning whole, sound, and uninjured.
items.cn: 古英语 hælth 出自 hal，意为「完整的、健全的、未受伤的」。

items.en: The root *hailaz meant whole or intact across the Germanic family.
items.cn: 词根 *hailaz 在日耳曼语族中意为「完整、完好」。

items.en: Old Norse heill, meaning good luck and soundness, reinforced the English sense.
items.cn: 古诺斯语 heill 意为「好运、健全」，强化了英语词义。

items.en: In Middle English, health also appeared in toasts, wishing others wholeness.
items.cn: 中古英语中 health 也出现在祝酒词里，祝愿他人安康。

items.en: Modern English built the medical sense, as in health care and public health.
items.cn: 现代英语发展出医疗义，如 health care、public health。

note.en: Look-alikes and meaning neighbours of health.
note.cn: health 的形近词与义近词。

entries.definitionCN: 健康的，同根形容词
治愈，同根动词
财富，拼写相近，词源不同

entries.definition: the state of being physically fit
entries.definitionCN: 健康；健身，偏重体能状态
幸福；健康安乐，范围更广

entries.definition: the state of being healthy and strong
entries.definitionCN: 健全，正式用语

normalIntro.en: Five ways to keep health in mind.
normalIntro.cn: 五个方式记住 health。

normal.cn: 同族词 heal（治愈）帮你锁定 health 的「完好」本义。
搭配「good health」（健康）是最常见的祝福语。
对比「health vs wealth」：wealth 换 h 为 w 才是财富。
短语「public health」（公共卫生）是高频搭配。
记住同根词 whole（完整）：健康就是完整无缺。

abstract.en: See a tree with full leaves after good care.
abstract.cn: 看见一棵精心照料后枝繁叶茂的树：完整而生机勃勃就是健康。

abstract.en: Feel a machine running smoothly without a rattle.
abstract.cn: 感受一台机器平稳运转、没有杂音：health 就是这种顺畅状态。

abstract.en: Raise a glass and wish wholeness for your friends.
abstract.cn: 举杯祝愿朋友「完整安康」：health 在祝词中的本义。

examples.en: Fresh air and exercise are good for your health.
examples.cn: 新鲜空气和锻炼有益健康。

examples.en: He gave up smoking to protect his health.
examples.cn: 为了保护健康，他戒了烟。

examples.en: The report examined the economic health of the region.
examples.cn: 报告评估了该地区的经济健康状况。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「海尔丝」——海尔兄弟「海尔丝」天天锻炼，身体 health（健康）。

root: health 来自古英语 hælth，源自日耳曼词根 *hailaz（完整、健全），与 whole（完整）、heal（治愈）同根。词义从「完整无缺的身体状态」延伸到机构与系统的运行状况，再扩展到医疗领域。

sensesIntro.en: From wholeness of the body to wholeness of systems.
sensesIntro.cn: 从身体的完好到系统的完好。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a flourishing tree after good care
core.cn: 核心意象：悉心照料后枝繁叶茂的树

branches.en: A body and mind in good order
The field of treating and preventing illness
branches.cn: 治疗与预防疾病的领域
运转良好的身体与系统同为一义

intro.en: Health heads a family of wholeness words.
intro.cn: health 是「完好」词族的核心。

latinIntro.en: Health is Germanic, so no Latin relatives appear here.
latinIntro.cn: health 属日耳曼词源，没有拉丁同族词。

definition_zh: 健康的；有益健康的；健全的
definition_en: physically strong and well; good for your health
core_image: 晨跑后出汗的少年：面色红润、呼吸有力
scene: 她每天早餐吃鸡蛋、牛奶和水果，课间还去操场跳绳。She stays healthy by eating well and exercising every day.
sceneCN: 这里 healthy 是「健康的」（第 1 个义项：身体状态良好）；她靠饮食和锻炼保持良好状态，healthy 正是描述这种状态的形容词。

derivatives.zh: 健康，healthy 的基础名词
健康地，由 healthy 加副词后缀 -ly 构成
健康状态，由 healthy 加名词后缀 -ness 构成

senses.title: Physically strong and well
senses.definition: strong and free from illness
senses.definitionCN: 强壮且没有疾病
senses.example: The doctor said the baby is perfectly healthy.
senses.exampleCN: 医生说这个宝宝非常健康。
senses.why: Health means good condition, and the suffix -y turns that condition into a description of a person or animal.
senses.whyCN: health 表示良好状态，后缀 -y 把这种状态变成对人或动物的描述，于是有「健康的」。

senses.title: Good for your health
senses.definition: likely to make you healthy
senses.definitionCN: 可能使你健康的
senses.example: Vegetables are part of a healthy diet.
senses.exampleCN: 蔬菜是健康饮食的一部分。
senses.why: Anything that keeps the body in good condition earns the same label, so food, habits, and air can all be healthy.
senses.whyCN: 凡能维持身体良好状态的东西都配得上这个标签，于是食物、习惯、空气都可以 healthy。

senses.title: Sound and thriving
senses.definition: showing that a system or organization is working well
senses.definitionCN: 表明系统或组织运行良好
senses.example: The company shows healthy growth this year.
senses.exampleCN: 公司今年显示出健康的增长。
senses.why: A well-running body maps onto a well-running organization, so growth and finances can also be healthy.
senses.whyCN: 运转良好的身体映射到运转良好的组织，于是增长与财务也可以「健康」。

intro.en: Healthy is simply health plus the common adjective suffix -y.
intro.cn: healthy 就是 health 加常见形容词后缀 -y。

items.en: The base word health comes from Old English hælth, meaning wholeness and soundness.
items.cn: 基础词 health 来自古英语 hælth，意为「完整、健全」。

items.en: The root *hailaz meant whole and intact across Germanic languages.
items.cn: 词根 *hailaz 在各日耳曼语言中表示「完整、完好」。

items.en: In Middle English, the suffix -y (from Old English -ig) formed adjectives of quality.
items.cn: 中古英语中，后缀 -y（源自古英语 -ig）用来构成表示性质的形容词。

items.en: Healthy and healthful competed for centuries before healthy became standard.
items.cn: healthy 与 healthful 竞争数百年，最终 healthy 成为标准。

items.en: Modern English extended healthy to food, economies, and organizations.
items.cn: 现代英语把 healthy 扩展到食品、经济与组织。

note.cn: healthy 的形近词与义近词。

normal.cn: 结构「health + -y」：健康状态加形容词后缀。
搭配「stay healthy」（保持健康）是最常用短语。

短语「healthy diet」（健康饮食）锁定第二义项。
同族词 heal、whole 帮你理解「完好即健康」。

abstract.en: See a boy running in the morning sun with red cheeks.
abstract.cn: 看见男孩在晨光中奔跑、脸颊红润：这就是 healthy 的画面。

abstract.en: Feel fresh salad filling you with energy.
abstract.cn: 感受一盘新鲜沙拉给你注入能量：有益健康的食物也是 healthy。

abstract.en: Watch a chart climbing steadily year after year.
abstract.cn: 看着图表逐年稳步上升：健康的增长曲线同样 healthy。

examples.en: She is healthy and full of energy every day.
examples.cn: 她每天都很健康、精力充沛。

examples.en: A healthy breakfast helps you focus at school.
examples.cn: 健康的早餐帮助你在学校集中注意力。

examples.en: The bank reported healthy profits this quarter.
examples.cn: 这家银行本季度报告了健康的利润。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「海尔戒」——海尔兄弟「海尔戒」掉零食，马上变得 healthy（健康）。

definition_en: to notice sounds with your ears; to be told about something
core_image: 耳朵竖起的雷达：声波撞进来就被捕捉
scene: 深夜的走廊很静，隔壁房间钢琴声一点点飘过来。She stopped to hear the music coming from the next room.
sceneCN: 这里 hear 是「听见」（第 1 个义项：用耳朵察觉声音）；她停下脚步捕捉琴声，hear 强调声音进入耳朵的结果。

derivatives.zh: 听力；听觉，由 hear 加后缀 -ing 构成
听者，与 hear 同义场的 listen 加后缀构成
听众，拉丁同义源词，与 hear 意义对应

senses.title: To notice sound with the ears
senses.definition: to become aware of a sound through the ears
senses.definitionCN: 通过耳朵察觉声音
senses.example: I can hear birds singing outside the window.
senses.exampleCN: 我能听见窗外鸟儿在唱歌。
senses.why: The ear works like a receiver catching sound waves, so hear names the act of catching a sound.
senses.whyCN: 耳朵像接收声波的雷达，hear 命名的就是捕捉到声音这个动作。

senses.title: To listen and pay attention
senses.definition: to listen carefully to what someone says
senses.definitionCN: 认真听某人说话
senses.example: The judge heard both sides before deciding.
senses.exampleCN: 法官听取双方陈述后才做决定。
senses.why: Catching a sound becomes catching someone's words and arguments, so hear extends to formal listening.
senses.whyCN: 捕捉声音延伸为捕捉言语与论点，hear 由此覆盖正式的听取场合。

senses.title: To be told or learn about
senses.definition: to be told about or learn about something
senses.definitionCN: 被告知或了解到某事
senses.example: Have you heard the news about the school trip?
senses.exampleCN: 你听说学校旅行了吗？
senses.why: Sound carries information, so hearing becomes receiving news through talk.
senses.whyCN: 声音承载信息，听见便延伸为经由言谈接收消息。

intro.en: Hear is an old Germanic verb tied to the ear family of words.
intro.cn: hear 是古老的日耳曼动词，与 ear 词族相关联。

items.en: Old English had heran or hieran, meaning to hear and to obey.
items.cn: 古英语作 heran 或 hieran，意为「听见、听从」。

items.en: It comes from the Germanic root *hauzjan, related to the word for ear.
items.cn: 它来自日耳曼词根 *hauzjan，与「耳朵」一词相关。

items.en: Old Norse heyra is a close relative with the same meaning.
items.cn: 古诺斯语 heyra 是同义的近亲词。

items.en: In Middle English, hear and listen settled into their modern roles: catch and attend.
items.cn: 中古英语里 hear 与 listen 分工定型：前者表示听见，后者表示倾听。

items.en: Modern English kept the irregular past heard and added phrases like hear from and hear of.
items.cn: 现代英语保留了不规则过去式 heard，并发展出 hear from、hear of 等短语。

note.en: Look-alikes and hearing neighbours.
note.cn: hear 的形近词与听觉近邻。

normalIntro.cn: 五个方式把 hear 记牢。

normal.cn: 对比「hear vs listen」：hear 是结果，listen 是主动动作。
短语「hear from」（收到消息）是最常见搭配之一。
过去式 heard 不加 -ed，读音也变。
「hear of / hear about」都表示听说，程度略有不同。
hear 里藏着 ear：耳朵在词中，意义也在耳朵。

abstract.en: Picture radar ears catching sound waves.
abstract.cn: 想象雷达般的耳朵捕捉声波：hear 就是声波被接收的瞬间。

abstract.en: Let the sound turn into news in your mind.
abstract.cn: 让声音在心里变成消息：听见即得知。

abstract.en: Sit in court and take in both sides.
abstract.cn: 坐在法庭上听取双方陈词：hear 的庄重用法。

examples.en: Did you hear that strange sound last night?
examples.cn: 昨晚你听见那个奇怪的声音了吗？

examples.en: I heard from my old friend after five years.
examples.cn: 五年后我收到了老朋友的消息。

examples.en: The audience heard the singer perform three songs.
examples.cn: 听众听了歌手演唱三首歌。

definition_en: the organ that pumps blood; the center of feelings; the most important part
core_image: 胸腔里日夜跳动的不熄引擎：泵出生命也藏着感情
scene: 赛跑到终点，他把手按在胸口感受砰砰的跳动。His heart was beating fast after the race.
sceneCN: 这里 heart 是「心脏」（第 1 个义项：泵血器官）；赛跑后胸口砰砰跳动，heart 正指这个身体器官。

derivatives.zh: 衷心的，由 heart 与 felt 复合，表示发自内心的

senses.title: The organ that pumps blood
senses.definition: the organ in the chest that pumps blood around the body
senses.definitionCN: 胸腔中把血液泵送到全身的器官
senses.example: Exercise makes your heart stronger.
senses.exampleCN: 锻炼使你的心脏更强壮。
senses.why: The chest holds the body's pump, and the word names this vital muscle first.
senses.whyCN: 胸腔里装着身体的泵，这个词首先命名这块关键的肌肉。

senses.title: The center of feelings
senses.definition: the place where feelings are thought to live
senses.definitionCN: 被认为情感居住之处
senses.example: She thanked him with all her heart.
senses.exampleCN: 她全心全意地感谢他。
senses.why: Ancient people felt emotions in the chest, so heart became the home of love, courage, and sorrow.
senses.whyCN: 古人感到情绪在胸腔涌动，heart 于是成为爱与悲伤的居所。

senses.title: The most important part
senses.definition: the most central or important part of something
senses.definitionCN: 事物最中心或最重要的部分
senses.example: We walked to the heart of the old town.
senses.exampleCN: 我们走到了老城的中心。
senses.why: The heart sits at the center of the body, so any central place or idea can borrow the name.
senses.whyCN: 心脏位于身体中心，于是任何中心位置或要点都可借用此名。

senses.title: Courage or spirit
senses.definition: bravery and determination
senses.definitionCN: 勇敢与决心
senses.example: The team lost the match but never lost heart.
senses.exampleCN: 球队输了比赛，但从未失去斗志。
senses.why: Strong feelings power action, so heart also stands for the spirit that keeps you going.
senses.whyCN: 强烈的情感驱动行动，heart 也代表支撑你继续下去的精神。

intro.en: Heart is one of the oldest words in English, reaching back to the earliest Germanic.
intro.cn: heart 是英语最古老的词之一，可追溯到最早的日耳曼语。

items.en: Old English heorte meant the organ, the feelings, and the inner self at once.
items.cn: 古英语 heorte 同时表示器官、情感与内在自我。

items.en: It comes from the Germanic root *hertô, the standard word for heart in the family.
items.cn: 它来自日耳曼词根 *hertô，是该语族表示心脏的标准词。

items.en: Latin cor and Greek kardia are distant Indo-European relatives of the same root.
items.cn: 拉丁语 cor 与希腊语 kardia 是同一词根的印欧远亲。

items.en: Old Norse hjarta reinforced the English form after Viking contact.
items.cn: 维京接触后，古诺斯语 hjarta 强化了英语词形。

items.en: Modern English added many idioms, such as learn by heart and heart of gold.
items.cn: 现代英语发展出 learn by heart、heart of gold 等大量习语。

abstract.en: Feel your chest thump after running upstairs.
abstract.cn: 感受爬楼后胸口的咚咚跳动：heart 最初就是这颗泵。

abstract.en: Notice emotions rising in your chest, not your brain.
abstract.cn: 察觉情绪在胸腔涌起而非头脑：heart 是古人的情感中心。

abstract.en: See a map with a dot at the middle of the city.
abstract.cn: 看见地图上城市正中的那个点：heart 即中心。

examples.en: Doctors say a healthy heart needs regular exercise.
examples.cn: 医生说健康的心脏需要规律锻炼。

examples.en: He learned the whole poem by heart in one evening.
examples.cn: 他一个晚上就把整首诗背了下来。

examples.en: The small cafe is at the heart of campus life.
examples.cn: 这家小咖啡馆是校园生活的中心。

senses.title: Thermal energy in physics
senses.titleCN: 物理学意义上的热、热能
senses.definition: the energy that transfers from a warmer body to a cooler one, measured in joules
senses.definitionCN: 从较热物体传向较冷物体的能量，以焦耳计量
senses.example: The experiment measured how much heat the metal bar absorbed.
senses.exampleCN: 实验测量了金属棒吸收了多少热量。
senses.why: The physical sense is the modern, countable-in-laboratory version of the old quality 'being hot'.
senses.whyCN: 物理义是旧义「热的性质」在实验室里可计量的现代版本。

senses.title: Hot weather
senses.definition: a period of unusually high air temperature, especially in summer
senses.definitionCN: 气温异常偏高的一段时间，尤指夏季
senses.example: The heat kept the whole town indoors until evening.
senses.exampleCN: 高温让全镇的人一直躲在家里直到傍晚。
senses.why: Weather talk applied the mass noun to the air itself, so 'the heat' became a way to name a hot spell.
senses.whyCN: 谈天气时把这个不可数名词用到了空气上，「the heat」便成了指一段暑热的说法。

senses.title: A source of warmth
senses.titleCN: 供暖；炉火或暖气带来的温暖
senses.definition: warmth supplied by a fire, radiator or heating system
senses.definitionCN: 由炉火、暖气片或供暖系统提供的温暖
senses.example: They sat close to the stove because the heat reached only the front room.
senses.exampleCN: 他们坐得离炉子很近，因为热气只到得了前屋。
senses.why: A fire is both the hot thing and the warmth it gives off, so the same noun names the source and the effect.
senses.whyCN: 火既是热的东西，也是它散发的温暖，因此同一个名词兼指来源与效果。

senses.title: Body temperature and fever
senses.definition: the warmth of a living body, especially when it is higher than normal
senses.definitionCN: 活体的温度，尤指高于正常水平时
senses.example: The nurse checked the child for heat around the forehead.
senses.exampleCN: 护士摸了摸孩子的额头，看有没有发热。
senses.why: Living bodies produce warmth, so the noun moved from the fire to the body and then to illness.
senses.whyCN: 活体自己产生热量，名词便从炉火移到身体，再移到疾病上。

senses.title: Pungency in food
senses.definition: the sharp burning sensation given by chilli, pepper or mustard
senses.definitionCN: 辣椒、胡椒或芥末带来的尖锐灼烧感
senses.example: The heat of the sauce surprised everyone at the table.
senses.exampleCN: 酱汁的辣度让桌上所有人都吃了一惊。
senses.why: The sensation is literally a burning warmth on the tongue, so the temperature word was borrowed for taste.
senses.whyCN: 那种感觉本就是舌头上的灼热，于是温度词被借去形容味道。

senses.title: Intensity of feeling or pressure
senses.titleCN: 情绪或局势的激烈程度
senses.definition: the most intense part of an activity, argument or period of pressure
senses.definitionCN: 活动、争论或压力最激烈的阶段
senses.example: In the heat of the debate, nobody noticed the clock.
senses.exampleCN: 辩论最激烈的时候，没人去看钟。
senses.why: Strong feeling was pictured as a fire burning at its hottest, so 'in the heat of' marks the peak.
senses.whyCN: 强烈情绪被想象成烧得最旺的火，因此「in the heat of」标出最炽烈的顶点。

senses.title: A preliminary race
senses.definition: one of several earlier races whose winners go on to the final
senses.definitionCN: 决赛之前举行的若干场比赛，胜者进入决赛
senses.example: She won her heat and advanced to the final.
senses.exampleCN: 她赢下了自己的预赛，进入决赛。
senses.why: Each preliminary race was felt to 'heat up' the competitors; the sporting sense is a separate branch of the same noun.
senses.whyCN: 每场预赛都被看作让选手「热起来」的环节；这一体育义是同一名词的另一条分支。

senses.title: To make something warm
senses.definition: to raise the temperature of something so that it becomes warm or ready to use
senses.definitionCN: 提高某物的温度，使其变热或可以使用
senses.example: He heated the soup until it steamed.
senses.exampleCN: 他把汤加热到冒热气。
senses.why: The verb is the plain causative of the noun: to heat something is to put heat into it.
senses.whyCN: 动词是名词的普通使役形式：给某物加热，就是把热放进某物里。

intro.en: Heat is a native English word, not a borrowing. Old English had hǣtu 'heat' beside hāt 'hot', and the noun has kept the same shape in meaning for a thousand years.
intro.cn: heat 是英语本族词，不是借词。古英语在 hāt「热的」之外还有 hǣtu「热」，这个名词的含义千年来基本未变。

items.en: Hǣtu meant 'heat, warmth, the quality of being hot' and was formed from hāt 'hot'.
items.cn: hǣtu 意为「热、温暖、热的性质」，由 hāt「热的」构成。

items.en: The same stock appears in Old High German heizī and modern German Hitze, so the word is shared across the Germanic languages.
items.cn: 同一词源出现在古高地德语 heizī 与现代德语 Hitze，说明这个词在日耳曼语族内共用。

items.en: The usual reconstruction is the root *kai- 'heat', but this is a reconstructed form, not a recorded word.
items.cn: 通常把词根构拟为 *kai-「热」，但这是重构形式，不是有记录的实际词。

items.en: From the nineteenth century heat became a technical term for transferred thermal energy, and the older everyday senses remained beside it.
items.cn: 从 19 世纪起，heat 成为指传递热能的术语，而更早的日常义仍与它并存。

items.en: Source uncertain (deeper root only): the pre-Germanic origin rests on a reconstruction, and the first date of the sporting sense is recorded only loosely.
items.cn: 来源不确定（仅更深词根）：日耳曼语之前的来源建立在重构之上；体育义的最早年代也只有粗略记载。

note.en: Group one holds words that look or sound close to heat but come from other roots; group two holds words for warmth or temperature that differ in scope.
note.cn: 第一组是形近或音近但词根不同的词；第二组是表示温暖或温度、范围有别的词。

entries.definition: The grain, from Old English hwǣte; it contains the letters of heat but has no connection to warmth.
entries.definitionCN: 指小麦，来自古英语 hwǣte；字母与 heat 相近，但与「热」毫无关系。

entries.definition: To strike something, from Old English hittan; the vowel and the meaning both keep it apart from heat.
entries.definitionCN: 指击打，来自古英语 hittan；元音与词义都使它不同于 heat。

entries.definition: To pay attention to something, from Old English hēdan 'to guard, observe'; it is not related to heat.
entries.definitionCN: 指留意、注意，来自古英语 hēdan「看守、观察」；与 heat 不同源。

entries.definition: An old word for a non-Christian pagan, from Old English hǣthen; the shared letters hide a different origin.
entries.definitionCN: 旧时指非基督教的异教徒，来自古英语 hǣthen；相同的字母掩盖了不同的来源。

entries.definition: A moderate, comfortable degree of heat; heat itself can be far more intense or technical.
entries.definitionCN: 温和舒适的热度；heat 本身可以强烈得多，也可以作为技术术语。

entries.definition: The measured degree of hotness of a body or place, rather than the energy or the sensation.
entries.definitionCN: 物体或场所被测出的冷热程度，而非能量本身或主观感受。

entries.definition: A body temperature above normal caused by illness; heat is the wider word for any warmth.
entries.definitionCN: 疾病引起的异常体温升高；heat 是泛指一切热度的更宽泛的词。

entries.definition: The flame itself that produces heat; heat names the warmth or energy that the fire gives off.
entries.definitionCN: 指产生热的火焰本身；heat 指火焰释放出的温暖或能量。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: a real native root, real compounds and real collocations, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的英语本族词根、真实复合词与真实搭配，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Old English hǣtu 'heat' stands beside hāt 'hot', so the noun and the adjective have always travelled together.
normal.cn: 古英语 hǣtu「热」与 hāt「热的」并立，名词与形容词一直同行。

normal.en: Compounds mark the senses: heat wave, body heat, heat source, heat loss, heat transfer.
normal.cn: 复合词标出各义项：热浪、体温、热源、热量损失、热传递。

normal.en: The verb family runs heat, heats, heated, heating, heater.
normal.cn: 动词词族包括 heat、heats、heated、heating、heater。

normal.en: The phrase 'in the heat of' always points to the most intense moment of an activity.
normal.cn: 「in the heat of」这一短语总是指活动最激烈的那一刻。

normal.en: Sporting heats are early races that heat up the competition before the final.
normal.cn: 体育中的 heat 是决赛前让竞争「热起来」的预赛。

abstract.en: Picture a kettle that keeps singing until the whole kitchen feels warm.
abstract.cn: 想象一只一直鸣响的水壶，直到整个厨房都暖起来。

abstract.en: Picture an argument that gets hotter the longer it lasts, until words are all sparks.
abstract.cn: 想象一场越吵越热的争论，最后每句话都成了火星。

abstract.en: Picture a single coal carried from a fire into a cold room, still glowing in the hand.
abstract.cn: 想象一块从火里带到冷屋的炭，仍在手心发着光。

examples.en: The heat from the radiator dried the wet coats overnight.
examples.cn: 暖气片的热量一夜之间把湿外套烘干了。

examples.en: Add the spices only after the oil begins to heat.
examples.cn: 等油开始变热后再下香料。

examples.en: The runners were assigned to different heats by their qualifying times.
examples.cn: 选手按资格赛成绩被分到不同的预赛组。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「热特」——把东西放到火上热一热，热就出来了

root: 古英语 hǣtu「热」，由 hāt「热的」构成，属日耳曼语族，与古高地德语 heizī、现代德语 Hitze 同源；更深词根通常重构为 *kai-「热」，属重构形式，非实际记录词。无拉丁语同族来源。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one line: warmth is first a physical quantity, then the weather, a fire, a body, a burning taste, a peak of feeling, a preliminary race, and finally the act of making something warm.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿一条线索展开：热先是物理量，然后是天气、炉火、身体、灼烧的味觉、情绪的顶点、预赛，最后是给东西加热的动作。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a red stove bottom with oil beginning to bubble above it.
core.cn: 核心意象：烧红的锅底，上面的油开始冒泡。

branches.en: MEASURED ENERGY: physics turns the old quality into joules that can be counted.
branches.cn: 可计量的能量：物理学把旧时的性质变成可数的焦耳。

branches.en: WEATHER AND FIRE: the same noun names a hot spell and the warmth a stove gives out.
branches.cn: 天气与炉火：同一个名词既指一段暑热，也指炉子散出的温暖。

branches.en: BODY AND TONGUE: warmth becomes fever, then the burning of chilli.
branches.cn: 身体与舌头：热变成发热，再变成辣椒的灼烧。

branches.en: PEAK AND PRELIMINARY: feeling and sport both use heat for the stage that burns brightest.
branches.cn: 顶点与预赛：情绪与体育都用 heat 指烧得最旺的阶段。

branches.en: THE CAUSATIVE VERB: to heat is simply to put heat into something.
branches.cn: 使役动词：加热就是把热放进某物。

intro.en: Heat is a free English root that combines with particles and suffixes; the derived family is large and mostly transparent.
intro.cn: heat 是一个自由英语词根，可与小品词和后缀组合；派生词族庞大且大多一目了然。

latinIntro.en: The word is native Germanic and has no Latin source; Latin calor and its family are semantic parallels only, so no Latin entries are listed.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词是日耳曼本族词，没有拉丁语来源；拉丁语 calor 及其词族只是语义上的平行词，因此不列拉丁词条。

items.example: The heater clicked on at midnight.

items.meaning: the process or system of warming a building
items.example: Heating costs rose with the cold snap.
items.exampleCN: 寒潮一来，供暖费用就上涨了。

items.meaning: a long period of very hot weather
items.exampleCN: 这波热浪持续了十一天。

items.meaning: to warm an oven before using it
items.example: Preheat the oven to two hundred degrees.

items.meaning: to become or make too hot
items.example: The engine overheated on the long climb.
items.exampleCN: 发动机在长坡上过热了。

items.example: She reheated the rice for lunch.
items.exampleCN: 她把米饭重新热了一下当午饭。

definition_en: in a heavy way; with force or in large amounts
core_image: 大雨砸在屋顶上的声音：密集、用力、不停歇
scene: 窗外雷声滚滚，雨点噼里啪啦往下砸。It rained heavily all night long.
sceneCN: 这里 heavily 是「猛烈地、大量地」（第 1 个义项：以沉重剧烈的方式）；雨整夜下得又大又急，heavily 描述雨的强度。

senses.title: With great weight or force
senses.definition: with a lot of weight, force, or intensity
senses.definitionCN: 以很大的重量、力量或强度
senses.example: Snow fell heavily on the mountain road.
senses.exampleCN: 雪大量落在山路上。
senses.why: Heavy things press down hard, so doing something heavily means doing it with full force.
senses.whyCN: 重物向下压迫，heavily 做副词即表示以全力或高强度行事。

senses.title: In large amounts or degrees
senses.definition: in large quantities or to a great degree
senses.definitionCN: 数量大或程度深
senses.example: The city relies heavily on tourism.
senses.exampleCN: 这座城市严重依赖旅游业。
senses.why: Weight also measures amount: what presses down in quantity presses down in importance too.
senses.whyCN: 重量也衡量数量：数量上的沉重也意味着程度上的深，heavily 由此表示大量与深度。

intro.en: Heavily is the adverb form of heavy, an old English word of weight.
intro.cn: heavily 是 heavy 的副词形式，heavy 是个古老的英语重量词。

items.en: Old English hefig meant having great weight.
items.cn: 古英语 hefig 意为「有很重的分量」。

items.en: It comes from the Germanic root *habjan, related to the verb have and the idea of lifting.
items.cn: 它来自日耳曼词根 *habjan，与动词 have 及「举起」的概念相关。

items.en: In Middle English, heavy and hevy varied in spelling as the word spread.
items.cn: 中古英语中 heavy 与 hevy 等拼写并存。

items.en: The adverb heavily formed with the standard suffix -li.
items.cn: 副词 heavily 由标准后缀 -li 构成。

items.en: Modern English extended heavily to rain, breathing, weapons, and dependence.
items.cn: 现代英语把 heavily 扩展到雨、呼吸、武器与依赖。

note.en: Look-alikes and meaning neighbours of heavily.
note.cn: heavily 的形近词与义近词。

normalIntro.en: Five anchors for heavily.

normal.cn: 结构「heavy + -ly」：形容词变副词的基本规则。
搭配「rain heavily」（雨下得大）是最常见用法。
短语「breathe heavily」（沉重呼吸）锁定身体义。
搭配「rely heavily on」（严重依赖）记住程度义。
先记 heavy（重的），副词含义随之而来。

abstract.en: Hear rain hammering the roof without stopping.
abstract.cn: 听雨点不停砸打屋顶：heavily 的节奏就是密集用力。

abstract.en: Feel your shoulders sink under a heavy bag.
abstract.cn: 感受肩膀被重包压得下沉：沉重感即 heavily 的本源。

abstract.en: See a city map crowded with tourist icons.
abstract.cn: 看见城市地图上挤满旅游图标：依赖 heavily 即占比极高。

examples.en: It snowed heavily, and all the schools closed.
examples.cn: 雪下得很大，所有学校都停课了。

examples.en: After the race, he lay on the grass breathing heavily.
examples.cn: 赛跑结束后，他躺在草地上沉重地呼吸。

examples.en: This region depends heavily on farming for income.
examples.cn: 这个地区的收入严重依赖农业。

scene: 搬家那天，哥哥扛着装满书的纸箱爬楼梯，喘着粗气。He put down the heavy box and wiped his face.
sceneCN: 这里 heavy 是「重的」（第 1 个义项：分量大）；装满书的纸箱压得他喘气，heavy 直接描述物体的重量。

senses.title: Having great weight
senses.definition: weighing a lot; hard to lift or carry
senses.definitionCN: 分量大；难以举起或搬运
senses.example: The suitcase was too heavy for the child.
senses.exampleCN: 这个箱子太重，孩子提不动。
senses.why: Gravity pulls every object down, and the word names the pull you feel in your arms.
senses.whyCN: 重力把一切往下拉，这个词命名的是你手臂感到的那份拉力。

senses.title: More than usual in amount
senses.definition: greater than usual in amount or degree
senses.definitionCN: 数量或程度超过一般
senses.example: There was heavy traffic on the highway.
senses.exampleCN: 高速公路上车辆很多。
senses.why: Many things together press like one big weight, so crowds, rain, and smoking can all be heavy.
senses.whyCN: 许多东西合在一起像一个大重物压着，于是车流、大雨、烟瘾都可以 heavy。

senses.title: Forceful or intense
senses.definition: using or showing great force
senses.definitionCN: 使用或显示很大的力量
senses.example: The team came under heavy attack in the second half.
senses.exampleCN: 球队下半场遭到猛烈的进攻。
senses.why: A big weight hitting you strikes hard, so heavy extends to attacks, blows, and storms.
senses.whyCN: 大重物砸下来力量惊人，heavy 由此延伸到进攻、打击与风暴。

senses.title: Sad and serious
senses.definition: sad or serious in feeling
senses.definitionCN: 情绪上悲伤或严肃
senses.example: She spoke of the sad news with a heavy heart.
senses.exampleCN: 她怀着沉重的心情说起这个坏消息。
senses.why: Sadness feels like carrying a load, so feelings borrow the language of weight.
senses.whyCN: 悲伤像背负重物，情绪借用了重量的语言。

intro.en: Heavy comes from the same Germanic family as the verb have.
intro.cn: heavy 与动词 have 同属一个日耳曼词族。

items.en: Old English hefig meant weighing a lot, formed from hebban, to lift.
items.cn: 古英语 hefig 意为「分量重」，由动词 hebban（举起）派生。

items.en: The root *habjan connected lifting and holding, so heavy is literally what needs lifting.
items.cn: 词根 *habjan 把「举起」与「持有」相连，heavy 字面即「需要举起之物」。

items.en: Old Norse þungr replaced heavy in northern dialects for a time.
items.cn: 古诺斯语 þungr 一度在北方方言中取代了 heavy。

items.en: In Middle English, heavy won back its place and grew the sense of intense and sad.
items.cn: 中古英语里 heavy 夺回地位，并发展出「猛烈」与「忧伤」义。

items.en: Modern English widely uses heavy in traffic, rain, weapons, and mood.
items.cn: 现代英语把 heavy 广泛用于交通、雨、武器与心情。

note.en: Look-alikes and weight neighbours of heavy.
note.cn: heavy 的形近词与重量近邻。

abstract.en: Carry sad news like a stone in your chest.

senses.title: The back part of the foot
senses.definition: the rounded back part of the foot
senses.definitionCN: 脚掌后端的圆状部分
senses.example: His heel hurt after the long walk.
senses.exampleCN: 走了很长的路后，他的脚后跟疼。
senses.why: The foot ends in a rounded pad at the back, and the word names that pad directly.
senses.whyCN: 脚掌末端有个圆形的后垫，这个词直接命名这个部位。

senses.title: The back part of a shoe
senses.definition: the part of a shoe that supports the heel of the foot
senses.definitionCN: 鞋上支撑脚后跟的部分
senses.example: She bought a pair of shoes with low heels.
senses.exampleCN: 她买了一双低跟鞋。
senses.why: The shoe copies the foot, so its back part takes the same name.
senses.whyCN: 鞋模仿脚的形状，鞋的后端便沿用了同一个名字。

senses.title: A dishonorable person
senses.definition: a person who behaves badly, in older slang
senses.definitionCN: 行为恶劣的人，旧式俚语
senses.example: The villain in the old film was a real heel.
senses.exampleCN: 老电影里的反派真是个卑劣家伙。
senses.why: Kicking and trampling with the heel suggests disrespect, so the word became slang for a mean man.
senses.whyCN: 用脚跟踢踩暗含轻蔑，这个词于是成为贬损恶劣男人的俚语。

intro.en: Heel is an old body word shared across Germanic languages.
intro.cn: heel 是一个古老的身体词，遍布各日耳曼语言。

items.en: Old English had hela, meaning the back part of the foot.
items.cn: 古英语作 hela，意为脚掌的后端。

items.en: It comes from a Germanic root meaning to incline or lean backward, fitting the shape of the heel.
items.cn: 它来自日耳曼词根，意为「后倾」，正合脚跟的形状。

items.en: Old Norse hæll is a close relative with the same meaning.
items.cn: 古诺斯语 hæll 是同义的近亲词。

items.en: In Middle English, heel extended to the back part of shoes and stockings.
items.cn: 中古英语里 heel 延伸到鞋和袜子的后跟部分。

items.en: Modern English added idioms like Achilles' heel and head over heels.
items.cn: 现代英语发展出 Achilles' heel、head over heels 等习语。

note.en: Look-alikes and foot neighbours of heel.
note.cn: heel 的形近词与足部近邻。

entries.definitionCN: 治愈，与 heel 发音相同但词源不同
穿高跟鞋的，同根复合词
heel 的复数形式

entries.definition: the front part of the foot
entries.definitionCN: 脚趾，足部前端的对应词
脚掌，足底部位词
脚踝，足部上方关节

normalIntro.en: Five anchors for the word heel.
normalIntro.cn: 记住 heel 的五个锚点。

normal.cn: 同音对比「heel vs heal」：脚跟与治愈，拼写一字母之差。
搭配「high heels」（高跟鞋）记住鞋跟义。
习语「Achilles' heel」（致命弱点）源自希腊神话。
习语「head over heels」（神魂颠倒）记住倒栽意象。
脚趾 toe 在前、脚跟 heel 在后，一对好搭档。

abstract.en: Feel the back of your foot touch the ground first.
abstract.cn: 感受脚底后端先着地：heel 就是那个圆垫。

abstract.en: Tap a high heel on the floor and hear it click.
abstract.cn: 让鞋跟敲地听听脆响：鞋跟是脚跟的替身。

abstract.en: Picture a villain trampling with his boots.
abstract.cn: 想象恶人用靴子踩踏：heel 的俚语贬义由此而来。

examples.en: New shoes often rub the heel at first.
examples.cn: 新鞋刚开始常会磨脚后跟。

examples.en: She walked quickly on her high heels.
examples.cn: 她穿着高跟鞋快步走着。

examples.en: Public speaking was his Achilles' heel.
examples.cn: 当众演讲是他的致命弱点。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「希欧」——跳芭蕾「希欧」一声落地，先用脚后跟 heel 着地。

root: heel 来自古英语 hela，源自日耳曼词根「后倾」，与古诺斯语 hæll、荷兰语 hiel 同源。词义从脚跟扩展到鞋跟，再经踩踏意象引申出俚语贬义。

sensesIntro.en: From the back of the foot to the back of the shoe and a mean man.
sensesIntro.cn: 从脚底后端到鞋的后跟，再到俚语中的恶人。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: the rounded pad that lands last and lifts first
core.cn: 核心意象：最后着地又最先离地的圆垫

branches.en: One shape copied from foot to shoe
branches.cn: 从脚到鞋复制的同一种形状

intro.en: Heel builds a few practical compounds.
intro.cn: heel 构成少量实用复合词。

latinIntro.en: Heel is Germanic, so Latin relatives are absent here.
latinIntro.cn: heel 属日耳曼词源，没有拉丁同族词。

definition_en: how tall someone or something is; the distance from bottom to top
core_image: 从地面到头顶的那条垂直线：一卷从底拉到顶的皮尺
scene: 体检时护士让他脱鞋站直，把皮尺从地面拉到他头顶。The doctor measured his height against the wall.
sceneCN: 这里 height 是「身高；高度」（第 1 个义项：从底到顶的距离）；皮尺量出的地面到头顶的长度，正是 height 表示高度的用法。

derivatives.zh: 高的，height 的基础形容词
加高；加强，由 height 加动词后缀 -en 构成
非常；高度地，由 high 加副词后缀 -ly 构成

senses.title: The distance from bottom to top
senses.definition: the measurement of how tall a thing or person is
senses.definitionCN: 人或物从底到顶的量度
senses.example: The tree reaches a height of ten meters.
senses.exampleCN: 这棵树高达十米。
senses.why: A ruler dropped from the sky measures the vertical span, and the word names that span.
senses.whyCN: 一把从天而降的皮尺量出垂直跨度，这个词命名的就是这段距离。

senses.title: A place far above the ground
senses.definition: a place or position far above the ground
senses.definitionCN: 远离地面的位置
senses.example: Some birds can fly at great heights.
senses.exampleCN: 有些鸟能在高空飞行。
senses.why: The measured distance becomes a place at that distance, so heights are the far-up spots.
senses.whyCN: 量出的距离变成了位于该距离之处，heights 便是高远之地。

senses.title: The strongest point or degree
senses.definition: the time or level when something is strongest
senses.definitionCN: 事物最强的时刻或程度
senses.example: The storm was at the height of its power.
senses.exampleCN: 风暴正处于最强时刻。
senses.why: The top of a measure becomes the peak of an event, so the tallest point stands for the strongest time.
senses.whyCN: 量度的顶端变成事件的巅峰，最高点由此代表最强时刻。

intro.en: Height comes from high through one of English's strangest spelling journeys.
intro.cn: height 由 high 演变而来，经历了英语中最奇特的拼写旅程之一。

items.en: Old English had hiehthu, built on the adjective heah, meaning high.
items.cn: 古英语作 hiehthu，建立在形容词 heah（高）之上。

items.en: The root *hauhaz meant high across the Germanic languages.
items.cn: 词根 *hauhaz 在各日耳曼语言中表示「高」。

items.en: In Middle English, spellings like heighte and heghte competed for centuries.
items.cn: 中古英语中 heighte、heghte 等拼写竞争数百年。

items.en: The th ending was influenced by analogy with words like depth and width.
items.cn: th 词尾受 depth、width 等词类推影响。

items.en: Modern English fixed the spelling height, though the gh stays silent.
items.cn: 现代英语固定拼写为 height，尽管 gh 不发音。

note.en: Look-alikes and measure neighbours of height.
note.cn: height 的形近词与度量近邻。

entries.definitionCN: 加高；加强，同根动词
第八，拼写相近，词源不同
重量，与 height 常被一起记，词源不同
高，日常表达
海拔；高度，技术用语
顶点，与第三义项相近

normalIntro.en: Five anchors for the word height.
normalIntro.cn: 记住 height 的五个锚点。

normal.cn: 由 high（高）记 height（高度）：同根的名词形式。
拼写要点：ei 组合，结尾 th，gh 不发音。
类比记忆「depth、width、height」：都是「- th」量度词。
搭配「afraid of heights」（恐高）记住高处义。
短语「the height of summer」（盛夏）记住顶峰义。

abstract.en: See a tape measure pulled from floor to crown.
abstract.cn: 看见皮尺从地面拉到头顶：height 就是这条垂直线。

abstract.en: Look down from a cliff edge and feel the drop.
abstract.cn: 从崖边俯视感受落差：heights 是脚下遥远的距离。

abstract.en: Watch a storm peak at noon and fade.
abstract.cn: 看风暴在正午达到顶点再消退：height 即最强时刻。

examples.en: What is the height of that building?
examples.cn: 那栋楼有多高？

examples.en: She is of medium height with short hair.
examples.cn: 她中等身材，留着短发。

examples.en: He felt dizzy looking down from such a height.
examples.cn: 从这么高的地方往下看，他觉得头晕。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「海特」——巨人「海特」身高惊人，皮尺从脚底量到头顶量出他的 height。

root: height 来自古英语 hiehthu，由形容词 heah（高，源自日耳曼词根 *hauhaz）加名词后缀 -thu 构成。th 词尾受 depth、width 类推影响而定，gh 在现代拼写中不发音。与 high、heighten 同根。

sensesIntro.en: From measured distance to far-up places and peak moments.
sensesIntro.cn: 从量出的距离到高远之地与巅峰时刻。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a tape measure pulled from floor to crown
core.cn: 核心意象：从地面拉到头顶的皮尺

branches.en: The top of the ruler and the top of the storm
branches.cn: 皮尺顶端与风暴之巅同一逻辑

intro.en: Height anchors the vertical measure family.
intro.cn: height 是垂直量度词族的核心。

latinIntro.en: Height is Germanic, so no Latin relatives appear here.
latinIntro.cn: height 属日耳曼词源，没有拉丁同族词。

definition_en: a word you say when you meet someone or answer the phone
core_image: 见面时扬起的手和笑着的嘴：一个把距离拉近的声音
scene: 新学期第一天，小明走进教室挥手向大家问好。Hello, everyone! I am your new classmate.
sceneCN: 这里 hello 是「你好」（第 1 个义项：见面打招呼）；小明挥手向大家问好，hello 是最日常的问候语。

derivatives.zh: 你好（旧式拼法），hello 的历史变体拼写
喊叫，有学者认为与 hello 词源相关，指大声呼喊
问候，hello 所属的功能类别词

senses.title: A greeting on meeting
senses.definition: a word used to greet someone you meet
senses.definitionCN: 见到某人时用来问候的词
senses.example: Hello, Mr. Li! How are you today?
senses.exampleCN: 李老师好！您今天怎么样？
senses.why: Meeting someone needs a friendly opening sound, and hello fills that spot in modern English.
senses.whyCN: 见面需要一个友好的开场声音，hello 在现代英语中占据这个位置。

senses.title: Answering the phone
senses.definition: the word used when answering a telephone call
senses.definitionCN: 接电话时使用的词
senses.example: Hello? This is Wang speaking.
senses.exampleCN: 喂？我是小王。
senses.why: The greeting fits the phone because the voice replaces the smile: distance needs an audible wave.
senses.whyCN: 问候语适合电话，因为声音代替了微笑：距离需要听得见的挥手。

senses.title: Calling attention
senses.definition: a call used to attract someone's attention
senses.definitionCN: 用来吸引别人注意的喊声
senses.example: Hello! Is anyone home?
senses.exampleCN: 喂！家里有人吗？
senses.why: The same friendly shout works as a knock on a door, seeking a reply.
senses.whyCN: 同一声友好的喊叫像敲门一样寻求回应。

intro.en: Hello is a surprisingly young word with a famous telephone story.
intro.cn: hello 是个出奇年轻的词，还与电话有一段著名渊源。

items.en: It likely grew from ho and la, shouts meaning stop and there.
items.cn: 一般认为它由 ho 与 la 两声呼喊融合而来，意为「停下、在那儿」。

items.en: Similar calls like holla existed in German and Dutch before English adopted the word.
items.cn: 德语与荷兰语中早有 holla 等类似呼喊，之后英语吸收了该词。

items.en: Early spellings holla and hallo meant a shout to stop someone.
items.cn: 早期拼写 holla、hallo 表示喝令某人停下。

items.en: Thomas Edison popularized hello as the standard telephone answer in the late nineteenth century.
items.cn: 十九世纪末，爱迪生把 hello 推广为标准的电话应答语。

items.en: Today hello is the commonest greeting in spoken English worldwide.
items.cn: 如今 hello 是全世界英语口语中最常用的问候语。

note.en: Look-alikes and greeting neighbours of hello.
note.cn: hello 的形近词与问候近邻。

entries.definitionCN: hello 的旧式拼法
空心的，拼写相近，词源不同
hello 的英式旧变体
嗨，更随意的问候语
早上好，分时段问候语
嘿，招呼与唤起注意

normalIntro.en: Five anchors for the word hello.
normalIntro.cn: 记住 hello 的五个锚点。

normal.cn: 搭配「say hello」（打招呼）是最基本的用法。
接电话先说 hello，这是爱迪生定下的传统。
对比「hello vs hi」：hello 稍正式，hi 更随意。
词源故事「ho + la」：两声呼喊合成一声问候。
打招呼的动作与声音配对：挥手 + hello。

abstract.en: See a hand raised and a mouth smiling across the street.
abstract.cn: 看见街对面扬起的手和微笑的嘴：hello 就是拉近距离的声音。

abstract.en: Hear the phone ring and answer with one word.
abstract.cn: 听见电话铃响，用一个词接起：hello 就是电话的门铃回应。

abstract.en: Shout hello into an empty house and wait for an echo.
abstract.cn: 朝空屋喊一声 hello 等回音：唤起注意的用法。

examples.en: Hello, welcome to our school!
examples.cn: 你好，欢迎来到我们学校！

examples.en: She said hello to the neighbors every morning.
examples.cn: 她每天早晨都向邻居们问好。

examples.en: Hello? The line is very bad, can you hear me?
examples.cn: 喂？信号很差，你听得见吗？

dict_mnemonic.text: 「哈喽」——见面笑喊「哈喽」，hello 本身就是最常见的问候音。

root: hello 一般认为源自呼喊语 ho + la（停下、在那儿），经古法语与德语系 holla 等形式进入英语，早期拼写有 holla、hallo、hullo。十九世纪末因电话普及而定型为 hello。

sensesIntro.en: From a shout on the street to the world's commonest greeting.
sensesIntro.cn: 从街头的呼喊到世界上最常用的问候。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a raised hand and a smiling voice
core.cn: 核心意象：扬起的手与含笑的声音

branches.en: One voice for face and phone
branches.cn: 面对面与打电话共用的同一个声音

intro.en: Hello stands mostly alone but has variant spellings.
intro.cn: hello 大多独立使用，但有几种拼写变体。

latinIntro.en: Hello has no Latin relatives; its roots are street calls.
latinIntro.cn: hello 没有拉丁同族词，其源头是街头呼喊。

definition_en: to make it easier for someone to do something; aid
core_image: 摔倒时伸过来的那只手：把人从地上拉起来
scene: 同学书包的带子断了，课本散了一地，他马上蹲下去一本一本捡。He stopped to help his classmate pick up the books.
sceneCN: 这里 help 是「帮助」（第 1 个义项：为别人做事提供便利）；他蹲下帮忙捡书，help 描述这种伸出援手的行为。

derivatives.zh: 帮手；助手，由 help 加施动者后缀 -er 构成
有帮助的，由 help 加后缀 -ful 构成
无助的，由 help 加后缀 -less 构成

senses.title: To give assistance
senses.definition: to make it easier for someone to do something
senses.definitionCN: 使某人做事更容易
senses.example: Mom helped me wash the dishes.
senses.exampleCN: 妈妈帮我洗碗。
senses.why: A hand reaching down shortens your work, so help names any act that lifts the load.
senses.whyCN: 伸来的手缩短了你的工作，help 命名一切替你分担的行为。

senses.title: To make something better or easier
senses.definition: to make a situation or result better or easier
senses.definitionCN: 使局面或结果更好更容易
senses.example: Eating fruit helps keep you healthy.
senses.exampleCN: 吃水果有助于保持健康。
senses.why: Assistance applies to things as well as people, so good conditions help outcomes.
senses.whyCN: 援助对象不限人也可以是事，好的条件同样「帮助」结果。

senses.title: To serve food or oneself
senses.definition: to give food to someone or take food for yourself
senses.definitionCN: 给某人盛食物或自己取食物
senses.example: Help yourself to some cake.
senses.exampleCN: 随便吃点蛋糕吧。
senses.why: Serving food at the table helps guests fill their plates, so the word settled into meals.
senses.whyCN: 上菜帮助客人装满盘子，这个词于是固定在餐桌场合。

senses.title: A cry for assistance
senses.definition: a loud call for assistance
senses.definitionCN: 大声寻求援助
senses.example: The swimmer shouted Help! as he sank.
senses.exampleCN: 游泳者下沉时大喊救命。
senses.why: The action becomes the word shouted when you need the action at once.
senses.whyCN: 当急需要这个行为时，行为之名就变成呼喊之词。

intro.en: Help is a native English verb with old cousins across Germanic.
intro.cn: help 是英语本族动词，在日耳曼各语言中有古老亲戚。

items.en: Old English helpan meant to help and also to avail or benefit.
items.cn: 古英语 helpan 意为「帮助」，兼有「有益于」之义。

items.en: It comes from the Germanic root *helpan, shared with Gothic hilpan.
items.cn: 它来自日耳曼词根 *helpan，与哥特语 hilpan 同源。

items.en: Old Norse hjalpa is a close relative in the northern branch.
items.cn: 古诺斯语 hjalpa 是北方语支的近亲。

items.en: In Middle English, the old irregular past holp slowly gave way to helped.
items.cn: 中古英语中，旧的不规则过去式 holp 逐渐让位于 helped。

items.en: Modern English added helping hands, helpful hints, and the cry Help!
items.cn: 现代英语发展出 helping hands、helpful hints 及呼救声 Help!

note.en: Look-alikes and helping neighbours.
note.cn: help 的形近词与援助近邻。

entries.definitionCN: 帮手，同根派生词
有帮助的，同根形容词

entries.definition: a steering wheel of a ship
entries.definitionCN: 舵轮，拼写相近，词源不同
援助，较正式的同义词
协助，正式用语

entries.definition: to hold up or back up
entries.definitionCN: 支持；支撑，义场相邻

normalIntro.en: Five anchors for the word help.
normalIntro.cn: 记住 help 的五个锚点。

normal.cn: 搭配「help someone with」（帮某人做）锁定动词句型。
餐桌用语「help yourself」（请自便）记住第三义项。
结构「can't help doing」（忍不住）是高频句型。
呼救词「Help!」是行为之名的直接呼喊。
对比例 helpful（有益）与 helpless（无助），后缀定方向。

abstract.en: See a hand reach down when you fall.
abstract.cn: 想象摔倒时伸下来的那只手：help 就是拉一把。

abstract.en: Feel homework finish faster with a friend beside you.
abstract.cn: 感受朋友在旁作业做得更快：帮助让事情变容易。

abstract.en: Pass a plate and say help yourself.
abstract.cn: 递过盘子说请自便：帮助也发生在餐桌上。

examples.en: Could you help me carry these books?
examples.cn: 你能帮我搬这些书吗？

examples.en: A good night's sleep helps you study better.
examples.cn: 睡个好觉有助于你更好地学习。

examples.en: Bystanders called for help when the fire started.
examples.cn: 起火时路人立刻呼救。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「海尔普」——伙伴「海尔普」顺手拉了你一把，help 就是帮忙。

root: help 来自古英语 helpan，源自日耳曼词根 *helpan（帮助、有益），与哥特语 hilpan、古诺斯语 hjalpa 同源。古英语不规则过去式 holp 已被 helped 取代。词义从助人扩展到有助于、用餐招待与呼救。

sensesIntro.en: From pulling someone up to serving food and shouting for rescue.
sensesIntro.cn: 从拉人一把到盛饭待客，再到呼救。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand reaching down to pull you up
core.cn: 核心意象：把你从地上拉起来的手

branches.en: The shouted word for urgent aid
One hand, offered quietly or cried for
branches.cn: 同一只手，可以是默默伸出也可以是大声呼求

intro.en: Help grows a compact family of support words.
intro.cn: help 长出一个紧凑的援助词族。

latinIntro.en: Help is Germanic, so no Latin relatives belong here.
latinIntro.cn: help 属日耳曼词源，没有拉丁同族词。
